analysis.overall: It was a turbulent day marked by repeated spikes over 190–200 mg/dL that were followed by sharp drops into low territory. While average glucose was strong at 119 mg/dL, frequent correction stacking made target stability hard to maintain.

events.title: Afternoon spike and low
events.description: Glucose jumped to 207 mg/dL following a meal and multiple quick corrections, but the combined insulin action pushed readings down to a low of 55 mg/dL within an hour.

events.title: Evening meal roller coaster
events.description: After a late dinner spike to 195 mg/dL, repeated micro-corrections stacked up and triggered a crash down to 56 mg/dL by 11:00 PM.

events.title: Midnight rebound high
events.description: Glucose rebounded sharply to 198 mg/dL overnight following the late-evening low, taking a series of correction boluses over two hours to stabilize around 75 mg/dL.

events.title: Morning site change & peak
events.description: A pump unreachable warning and bolus delivery issue around a site change coincided with a peak reading of 212 mg/dL after breakfast.

events.title: Late morning correction drop
events.description: Seven separate 0.3u corrections over an hour brought a 201 mg/dL high down quickly, eventually drifting past target into a low of 54 mg/dL by early afternoon.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Notice how stacking multiple small correction boluses within 30-60 minutes consistently led to low readings 1-2 hours later throughout the day.
